images.alt_grc: ὁ Λύσις καὶ ὁ Μικίων ἐκ τοῦ Κεραμεικοῦ βαίνουσιν
images.alt_en: Winter 431/0: Lysis and Mikion walk home from the Kerameikos after the public funeral; ten wagons with cypress coffins, one for each tribe, stand empty by the road.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Δημόκριτος περὶ τοῦ Κλεισθένους λέγει
images.alt_en: Demokritos, the farmer who loves politics, counts off the ten tribes on his fingers for the two boys in a crowded street of the city.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Κλεισθένης τὴν χώραν διανέμει
images.alt_en: A schematic map of Attica divided into three regions, city, coast and inland, with one 'third' from each joined into a tribe (drawn in the style of a vase painting).

images.alt_grc: ἡ βουλή
images.alt_en: The Council: rows of citizens seated on the benches of the Council house (bouleuterion) listening to a speaker.
images.credit: placeholder (target: reconstruction drawing of the Athenian bouleuterion, CC BY)

images.alt_grc: οἱ ἐπώνυμοι
images.alt_en: The Monument of the Eponymous Heroes in the Athenian Agora: the long base where the ten tribal heroes stood and public notices were posted.
images.credit: placeholder (target: Wikimedia Commons photograph of the monument's remains, CC BY-SA)

images.alt_grc: ὁ Λύσις ὄστρακον ἐν τῷ ἐργαστηρίῳ εὑρίσκει
images.alt_en: In the workshop yard among heaps of broken pottery, Lysis holds up a sherd with scratched letters; grandfather Kleinias sits on a bench in the sun.

images.alt_grc: ὁ γεωργὸς τῷ Ἀριστείδῃ τὸ ὄστρακον δίδωσιν
images.alt_en: 482 BC in the Agora: a farmer with a hoe on his shoulder hands a potsherd to a quiet, plainly dressed man, Aristides, and asks him to write a name on it.

images.alt_grc: οἱ Ἀθηναῖοι ὀστρακίζουσιν
images.alt_en: The Agora fenced off for an ostracism: citizens file in tribe by tribe and drop their sherds; officials count the heap.

images.alt_grc: ὄστρακα
images.alt_en: Ostraka from the Athenian Agora, 480s BC, inscribed with the names of Themistocles son of Neocles, Aristides son of Lysimachus and others (Agora Museum, Athens).
images.credit: placeholder (target: Wikimedia Commons photograph of Agora Museum ostraka, CC BY-SA)

images.alt_grc: ὁ Εὔδημος πρῲ εἰς τὸ δικαστήριον σπεύδει
images.alt_en: Dawn in a crowded city street: Eudemos, a burly charcoal-burner in a rough cloak, hurries off with other old men towards the law courts; Lysis calls after him from the doorway.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Δημόκριτος καὶ ὁ Ἀρίστων διαλέγονται
images.alt_en: Evening by a lamp: Demokritos waves his hands and argues with Ariston over the table; Lysis listens, chin in hands.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Κίμων τὰ χωρία ἄφρακτα ἔχει
images.alt_en: Cimon's orchards without fences: villagers help themselves to figs and grapes while a steward watches, smiling.

images.alt_grc: τὸ πινάκιον
images.alt_en: A bronze juror's ticket (pinakion), 4th century BC, stamped with its owner's name, father's name and deme, and a letter for his jury section.
images.credit: placeholder (target: museum photograph of a bronze pinakion, CC0 / CC BY)

images.alt_grc: οἱ δικασταὶ τὰ πινάκια φέρουσιν
images.alt_en: Morning outside the law courts in the 4th century: citizens queue at ten entrances, each holding a small bronze ticket; a stone allotment machine stands at each entrance.

images.alt_grc: ὁ ἄρχων τοὺς κύβους εἰς τὸ κληρωτήριον ἐμβάλλει
images.alt_en: The archon pours white and black balls into the bronze tube of the kleroterion; a juror whose name has been called draws an acorn-token from a water jar and holds up its letter.

images.alt_grc: ὁ δικαστὴς τὴν βακτηρίαν λαβὼν βαδίζει
images.alt_en: A juror with a staff painted red walks towards a court doorway marked with the same red colour and the same letter; an attendant hands him a token.

images.alt_grc: κληρωτήριον
images.alt_en: Fragment of a marble kleroterion (allotment machine) with rows of ticket slots, 4th century BC, found in the Athenian Agora (Agora Museum).
images.credit: placeholder (target: Wikimedia Commons photograph of the Agora Museum kleroterion, CC BY-SA)

images.alt_grc: ὁ ἀδύνατος ἐν τῇ βουλῇ λέγει
images.alt_en: Inside the Council house: a grey-bearded craftsman leaning on two sticks speaks to rows of seated councillors; his accuser, arms folded, watches from the side.

images.alt_grc: ὁ ἀνὴρ ἐπὶ ἵππον ἀναβαίνει
images.alt_en: A lame man is helped up onto a borrowed horse in a city street; two men point and whisper.

images.alt_grc: ὁ ἀνὴρ ἐν τῷ ἐργαστηρίῳ χαλεπῶς ἐργάζεται
images.alt_en: The old craftsman at work alone in his small shop, bent over his bench, with no apprentice beside him.

images.alt_grc: ἀνὴρ βακτηρίᾳ χρώμενος
images.alt_en: Attic marble grave relief, 4th century BC: a man leaning on his staff.
images.credit: placeholder (target: Metropolitan Museum of Art open access (CC0))

images.alt_grc: οἱ τριάκοντα ἐν τῇ πόλει ἄρχουσιν
images.alt_en: 404 BC: thirty grim men in fine cloaks sit on a platform in the Agora; Spartan soldiers with red cloaks stand guard behind them.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Θέογνις καὶ ὁ Πείσων περὶ τῶν μετοίκων λέγουσιν
images.alt_en: Two of the Thirty whisper together over a list of names; one taps it with his finger, the other smiles.

images.alt_grc: τὸν Λυσίαν ξένους ἑστιῶντα καταλαμβάνουσιν
images.alt_en: Armed men burst into a dining room where Lysias reclines with guests; the guests are pushed out of the door while Lysias is seized.

images.alt_grc: ἐργαστήριον χαλκέων
images.alt_en: A bronze workshop on an Attic red-figure cup (the Berlin Foundry Cup, c. 490–480 BC): craftsmen working on a bronze statue, with tools and helmets hanging on the wall.
images.credit: placeholder (target: Wikimedia Commons photograph of the Berlin Foundry Cup, CC BY-SA)

images.alt_grc: ἀσπίς
images.alt_en: A bronze hoplite shield of the late 5th century BC: the Spartan shield captured at Pylos in 425 and hung up in the Athenian Agora (Agora Museum).
images.credit: placeholder (target: Wikimedia Commons photograph of the Pylos shield, Agora Museum, CC BY-SA)

images.alt_grc: ὁ Φίλιππος πολλὰς πόλεις αἱρεῖ
images.alt_en: 351 BC: Macedonian cavalry and a phalanx with long pikes before the walls of a northern Greek town; King Philip, bearded, one eye bandaged, rides at their head.

images.alt_grc: οἱ Ἀθηναῖοι ἐν τῇ ἀγορᾷ πυνθάνονται εἴ τι καινὸν λέγεται
images.alt_en: Athenians strolling in the Agora under a stoa, gossiping in little groups and asking a traveller for news.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Δημοσθένης ἐν τῇ Πυκνὶ λέγει
images.alt_en: Demosthenes, a thin intense man, speaks from the stone platform of the Pnyx to thousands of seated citizens, one hand raised.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Δημοσθένης
images.alt_en: Portrait bust of Demosthenes, Roman marble copy of the bronze statue by Polyeuktos set up in Athens in 280 BC.
images.credit: placeholder (target: Wikimedia Commons photograph (Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek or Louvre copy), CC BY / PD)
